title: NDJSON stream contract
detail: The worker reads JSON objects line by line; stream_start and raw payloads are persisted. Contract version and PID remain in raw payloads.

title: Progress and surface completions
detail: Typeless numeric step lines and run_end, test_md_done, testrun_done, remote_done, and explore done are recognized. Complete remote session paths and Test Manager metadata remain in the payload rather than dedicated ledger columns.

title: Confirmed product-bug classification
detail: Result code 740 and its verdict are stored separately from exit code 1. An ordinary failed assertion is not sufficient proof of a confirmed product bug.

title: Unresolved variable warnings
detail: Warning payloads retain variables, reasons, used_by and suggested_file. The theater displays missing names and the suggested file.

title: Sealed evidence archive
detail: The worker finds packs, records validation status and digest, and uploads when storage is configured. The upstream tree contains no authentic committed packs.

title: Local evidence viewing
detail: A genuine uploaded pack can be downloaded and opened with evidence serve. The command requires a real pack and local CLI.

title: Evidence merge and policy gates
detail: Policy IDs are supported for authored and batch runs. Receipt signing requires validated evidence and a passing configured policy. A merged desktop-plus-mobile pack is not implemented.

title: Reusable testmd and cached replay
detail: Testmd jobs and reusable authored specifications are supported. The checkout template includes a shared helper. No authentic output cache is committed; replaying UI events is not native cached testmd execution.

title: Noninteractive batch suites
detail: The worker assembles testrun run with tags, paths, parallel workers, --agent and closed stdin. Live behavior remains dependent on the installed CLI and account.

title: Extracted final state
detail: run_end.final_state is stored as JSONB and shown in the run inspector.

title: Network checkpoints
detail: Plain-English objectives and specs can request network checks. The worker reads HAR/NDJSON records and retains failures; live status assertions cannot be certified from the code alone.

title: Console checkpoints
detail: Console slices, errors, and warnings are inspected. Unpacked data is bounded, so the UI is not an unlimited console archive.

title: Core Web Vitals
detail: Specs can request LCP and CLS checks. There is no structured collector for all LCP, CLS, INP, and TTFB measurements. An objective mentioning a metric is not a measured result.

title: Cookie security assertions
detail: The test specification requests httpOnly, secure, and sameSite checks. No authentic cookie result was available in this environment.

title: Storage, clipboard, and conditional steps
detail: The authored checkout template includes cart-state, clipboard, state extraction, and conditional test-environment verification. These are specifications, not passing evidence.

title: Append-only Assurance context
detail: The repository stores current requirement snapshots in PostgreSQL. No committed, Kane-created .context history or context review approval proves the proposed build-time Assurance layer.

title: Requirement trust states
detail: Derived, trusted, and stale claims are modeled. Updating a Markdown specification reconciles its claims. Generating a test is not treated as a successful execution.

title: Two-axis coverage
detail: The UI maps claims to specifications and displays trusted/active requirement coverage. The worker can request cover gaps --json. This is not a complete two-axis Test Manager reporting implementation.

title: Suite drift reconciliation
detail: A signed docs-change webhook requests maintain reconcile --plan and cover gaps. No automatic approval of new requirements or complete CLI context lifecycle is proven.

title: Multi-browser exploration
detail: The worker supports explore run --url. There is no confirmed 20-browser run, exploration-map import through explore context, or guaranteed cloud concurrency.

title: Remote HyperExecute grid
detail: Remote suite dispatch is present. Device-name flags do not change a web member into a device member; correct target frontmatter, app artifacts, plugin, credentials, and entitlement are prerequisites.

title: Real Android and iOS devices
detail: Android real-device arguments and an iOS simulator selection exist. A real iOS app/session workflow and uploaded, tested mobile application are not supplied.

title: Official GitHub Action
detail: The repository implements a webhook and Docker worker, not a checked-in LambdaTest/kane-cli-run workflow.

title: Chrome CDP cold starts
detail: The container sets an explicit Chrome path, skip-download flag, 60000 ms CDP timeout and two retries. A live cold-start timing measurement is not present.

title: Render execution plane
detail: Dockerfile and Render service blueprint are present. A deployed worker, remaining promotional balance, zero-cost operation and availability SLA are external matters.

title: Realtime transport and latency
detail: Run updates use PostgreSQL-backed SSE and workspace polling. There is no Supabase Realtime channel token or demonstrated sub-100ms latency.

title: Storage and pack unpacking
detail: Optional Supabase Storage upload, screenshots, console, HAR and failure.yaml are implemented. Extraction is into a temporary directory, not in memory; no bucket is provisioned by this repository.

title: Credit conservation
detail: Instant replay consumes no live credits. Native testmd cache reuse requires actual recorded files. A shallow repository checkout does not persist new caches between worker jobs.

title: Read-only Assurance commands
detail: cover gaps is requested for docs audits. A complete fsck and design explain pipeline and exhaustive zero-credit assertions are not established.

title: Groq and Gemini repair providers
detail: Server-side provider clients and an evidence-informed patch proposal path exist. No paid/free model execution was performed and current free-tier quotas were not verified.

title: Three qualification bars
detail: Each bar needs a real end-to-end run, genuine proof, and an actual agent/referee exchange. Only live runs with sealed evidence count.

title: Verified tie-breaker
detail: The UI exposes inspectable evidence. Judging weight and award decisions are not software invariants or independently confirmed by this audit.

title: Closed-loop tie-breaker
detail: The state machine exists in code; a successfully deployed live loop requires worker, repository, model and signing credentials. A Chaos Lab battle has been executed end to end against real TestMu credentials.

title: Triple-layer Kane integration
detail: Runtime orchestration and post-mortem self-verification are implemented paths. Build-time requirement approval and 100% verified project coverage are not proven.

title: Patch-intent auditing
detail: The anti-cheat auditor checks file scope, test edits, removed validation and known fixture literals. It is heuristic text analysis, not an AST proof of semantic correctness.

title: HMAC receipts
detail: Canonical signed JSON binds run IDs, commit, timestamp and the stored validated pack digest. Missing/malformed digests and failed validation are rejected. This is not independent re-hashing of an external file on every GET.

title: Judge fallback
detail: Recorded runs replay instantly from stored NDJSON events without credits. Live records replay through SSE. The five requested genuine sealed archives and byte-for-byte stdout storage are absent; JSONB preserves events rather than original whitespace.

title: Meetups and follow-up
detail: Meetup dates and participation are outside the application and have not been independently established.

title: B2B billing and tenancy
detail: Credit budgets and a team roster exist. The control plane is single-workspace: team roles are not tenant isolation. There is no subscription billing, tenant-scoped RLS, or demonstrated willingness to pay.

title: Public launch posts
detail: Share snippets are available, but there are no verified public launch links, published engagement metrics, or submitted four-minute video. No social post was published on the operator’s behalf.

title: Concept selection
detail: CHAOS-PACT is the implemented concept. DOC-TRUTH-ENGINE and SHADOW-OPS are comparison alternatives, not additional products that must be deployed.

title: Lightweight browser control plane
detail: Next.js and PostgreSQL serve data and views. The browser does not run Chrome automation, Xcode, or an Android emulator. Live execution is separated into the worker.

title: Authentication and balance preflight
detail: whoami, optional noninteractive login, and balance are present. A human-readable balance is parsed; account limits and exact remaining credits require a live account.

title: Flow branches and completed step counts
detail: Raw startup/unknown events are retained. Child IDs distinguish parallel steps, and done/failed transitions are counted instead of treating the highest step as a count.

title: Terminal and exit-code semantics
detail: The ledger distinguishes pass, failure, infrastructure error and timeout/cancellation. Not every exit 1 means a product bug: suites can break, and policy failures differ from application regressions. Automatic doctor recovery is not a complete workflow.

title: Evidence discovery and integrity
detail: stderr hints and session/project directories are searched. Validation/digest checks guard receipt publication. File-name-based extraction still depends on archive layout; interoperability must be exercised with real packs.

title: Composable checkout specification
detail: The repository now includes an authored six-domain template, shared helper, and a platform smoke specification. Configure owned staging URLs and test fixtures before execution. No live cache or evidence is fabricated.

title: Explore and baseline stage
detail: An EXPLORE state exists, but it does not establish a full accepted baseline and 20-browser map on every battle.

title: Adversarial arena and referee
detail: The original worker/branch workflow is preserved. The owned Chaos Lab target lets the Red team break a real page without touching any repository.

title: Repair attempts and escalation
detail: MAX_ATTEMPTS is three, with BLOCKED_NEEDS_HUMAN escalation. Patch checks and re-verification exist; there is no claimed proof of root-cause correctness, multi-worker race freedom, or full multi-target evidence merging.

title: Self-verifying publication
detail: Drafting, HMAC signing, a self-check request and the verification-to-publication transition exist. Editing a draft invalidates its previous verifier run.

title: Core schema and additive recovery
detail: All six core tables plus settings and team roster are defined. The committed Drizzle baseline and a transaction-scoped advisory lock repair missing tables and columns without dropping existing rows. Incompatible types and unfillable legacy fields require operator migration.

title: Production tenant isolation
detail: There is no organization key on the six core tables and no per-tenant PostgreSQL policies. A private single-tenant deployment is not a multi-tenant SaaS.

title: Unified execution dispatcher
detail: POST /api/kane/trigger accepts project-scoped replay and dispatches live jobs per target. It returns SSE URLs, not Supabase subscription tokens.

title: GitHub PR and documentation gates
detail: HMAC webhook verification, PR smoke jobs, reconciliation, and comments exist. PR smoke dispatch is desktop by default. Full git bisect, exact breaking-line attribution, check-run branch enforcement, and delivery deduplication are not implemented.

title: Arena request boundary
detail: Scenario validation and isolated-branch orchestration exist upstream. The Chaos Lab target avoids any remote mutation.

title: Evidence-guided healer
detail: Repair input includes failure context, logs, repository sources, and fixture values. It is not a guaranteed multimodal or AST-based repair, and requires external services for live operation.

title: Incident post-mortem generator
detail: Articles and social snippets are generated from the ledger. A passing live re-verification and validated evidence are required before signing. The full publication path was not exercised with real Kane credentials.

title: Public receipt JSON and SVG
detail: Battle or linked run IDs resolve to JSON receipts or an SVG badge. Verification rechecks HMAC and stored digest.

title: Four-minute demonstration
detail: The storyboard is a plan, not a recording. A successful demo, real mobile run, and 45-second qualification proof cannot be inferred from the interface.

title: Live worker safeguards
detail: Per-requester guards and reported balance checks exist. A ready remote account, durable job queue, global atomic credit reservations, sustained concurrency, and uptime remain deployment work.

title: Launch kit and publishing authorization
detail: HN, X, Reddit and LinkedIn templates are not evidence of publication. No engagement, award eligibility, pricing promise, or future event is certified.

title: Schema-aware readiness
detail: Health probes all columns in all eight tables. A reachable server with an incompatible schema no longer passes as a healthy workspace.

title: Dashboard outage isolation
detail: Database errors are sanitized. A disconnected workspace keeps a labelled read-only view and retry action rather than exposing SELECT statements on every route.

title: Reproducible Vercel build
detail: The standard Next.js preset uses npm ci and npm run build. The build no longer rewrites tsconfig; the migration is traced into server functions. Hosted deployment still needs the owner’s Vercel/Postgres configuration.
